subject: Scale bridge: term & capacity adjustments for renewal
messages:
From: Daniel Lowe <daniel@greenfieldanalytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal coming up — need a short-term capacity/onramp plan

Hi Sergio,

Our current Redwood agreement renews at the end of August and usage has been trending up faster than we modeled — Q2 token consumption is ~1.8x our expectation. We want to avoid a hard cap during the quarter while we finalize our product changes.

Can Redwood offer a short-term bridge for Aug–Oct (6–8 weeks) that: 1) holds the current effective rate while we ramp; 2) provides burst credits or a temporary burst pool; and 3) leaves open a longer-term commit decision before the end of the calendar year.

If you can outline 2–3 options (e.g., temporary price hold + burst pool; short-term uplift commit with credits; or a moderate discount for an accelerated 12-mo commit), that would be helpful. I can pull in procurement if we have a clear path.

Thanks — would prefer a quick call next week.

—Daniel
Director of Platform Engineering
Greenfield Analytics
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Lowe <daniel@greenfieldanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — need a short-term capacity/onramp plan

Daniel — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the growth. Looping in Lauren (finance) and Monica (CS) so we can put together concrete alternatives.

High-level we can structure three practical options that balance cost predictability and runway:

- Option A: 12-month renewal (starts 9/1) with a graded discount ladder and one-time onboarding credit to offset the Q3 ramp. Good for predictable pricing + longer-term commitment.
- Option B: 3–4 month bridge (Aug–Nov) with a price hold at your current rate + a temporary burst pool (pre-purchased credits usable for overages). We can cap burst unit consumption and provide a one-time burst credit to smooth the immediate ramp.
- Option C: 6-month uplift commit with an introductory uplift discount and a prorated credit carve-out; after 6 months we re-evaluate and either convert to a 12-month commit or allow a true-up.

I attached our Q2 usage extract and an internal preliminary term-options PDF to help drive the numbers.

If you’re available I can do a 30-min sync on Wednesday 6/28 or Friday 6/30.

Attachments: usage-summary-q2.csv (CSV extract), proposed-term-options.pdf (internal draft)

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing note — Greenfield bridge alternatives

Sergio / Monica,

I ran the numbers against the usage extract Sergio attached. Quick notes:

- Bridge (Option B) — low operational friction. Recommend: price hold at current effective rate, sell a 200k token burst pool ($Xk) with a 6-week expiration plus 50k complimentary burst credit to start. This keeps list pricing unchanged while preserving G&A for scaling.
- 6-month uplift (Option C) — better economics if they convert. Recommend: 10% uplift discount on the incremental committed units (not retroactive) and one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of the uplift value.
- 12-month (Option A) — we can offer a step-down discount (8% year one, 6% year two) but only if they commit to a minimum monthly floor.

I attached a quick pricing-matrix that models these scenarios. If we send Option B as the quick path, we should still include a 30-day review clause to convert to Option C with credit rollover.

Let me know if you want me to draft the outbound proposal.

Attachments: pricing-matrix-v3.xlsx

—Lauren
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Lowe <daniel@greenfieldanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: short bridge + burst pool (three options enclosed)

Daniel — appreciate the patience. Per our sync last week attached is a customer-facing proposal that lays out the three options we discussed (Option A / B / C) with pricing examples and next steps.

Summary (top-line):
- Your ask: avoid a hard cap during Q3 while you onboard new models and finish the product release.
- Recommended quick path (Option B): 2-month bridge starting 2028-08-01 with a price hold at your current effective rate and a pre-purchased burst pool (200k tokens) + 50k complimentary burst credit. This is designed to buy time and keep your effective unit cost unchanged during the immediate ramp.
- Conversion path: include a 30-day review window to convert bridge credits into a 6-month uplift commit (Option C) with credit rollover mechanics, or elect a 12-month renew with a step discount (Option A).

I’ve attached the customer proposal PDF and included a DocuSign link for a short-term amendment if you want to lock Option B today. If you prefer, we can run the bridge first and finalize the longer-term commit after the 30-day review.

Attachments: Greenfield-proposal-0708.pdf
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/sign/ABC-GF-0708

Would you like to lock Option B or schedule a 30-min call to walk through the fine points?

Best,
Sergio
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
From: Daniel Lowe <daniel@greenfieldanalytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@greenfieldanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: short bridge + burst pool (three options enclosed)

Sergio — thanks for the clear options. We’re aligned with Option B (bridge + burst pool) and want to proceed, subject to two small items: 1) can the complimentary burst credit be extended to 90 days instead of 60; and 2) can we add a one-month trial of elevated KV-cache capacity to ensure latency during the model roll-out (we can attach a quick performance SLA to that trial).

If you can confirm those two changes, Procurement is ready to sign the short amendment. Please send the updated amendment and I’ll get the DocuSign started.

On the last call you mentioned a one-page amendment draft; could you send that to procurement and cc me?

—Daniel
Director of Platform Engineering
Greenfield Analytics
